content.content:
1	# Refresh strategy
2	
3	When the user runs `/resell-au refresh <folder>`, the skill enters
4	**Refresh Mode** — a third top-level mode alongside Text Mode and
5	Folder Mode. Refresh Mode delete-and-relists stale FB Marketplace
6	listings to reset the FB algorithm's "honeymoon" visibility window.
7	
8	This file is the single home for refresh-only reference detail. Phase
9	index (all sections live below):
10	
11	| Phase | What it does | Where to read |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| R0 | Discovery & classification (read-only) — candidate table, session cap, floor gate | § "Phase R0 — discovery & classification" |
14	| R1 | Delete existing listing on FB | `browser-automation.md` § "Refresh Mode — Phase R1 delete loop"; locators in `facebook-marketplace.md` § "Delete listing locators" |
15	| R2 | Recreate at new price + update `listing.md` | § "Phase R2 — recreate at new price"; scripts: `refresh_listing_md_update.py`, `refresh_pricing.py` |
16	| Multi-item loop | Session cap, inter-item delays, resume on restart | § "Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop"; script: `refresh_runstate.py` |
17	| R3 | Summary table | § "Phase R3 — summary output" |
18	
19	## Why delete-and-relist
20	
21	FB Marketplace gives every new listing a 24–48 hour "honeymoon" of
22	aggressive feed visibility. After a few days, visibility drops sharply.
23	The established reseller tactic — confirmed across 2024–2026
24	reseller-community research — is to **delete the stale listing and
25	recreate it with a fresh price.** Empirically this produces a ~30%
26	message-rate lift vs the native "Renew" button.
27	
28	Trade-off: deleting loses **saves, chat history, and view count.** The
29	skill prints a one-line data-loss warning at the top of Phase R0 so
30	the user is reminded before confirming the candidate table.
31	
32	## Phase R0 — discovery & classification
33	
34	Phase R0 is read-only: walk the target folder, parse each subfolder's
35	`listing.md`, and produce a candidate table. No browser actions in
36	this phase other than the existing Chrome login check from Folder Mode
37	Phase 0.
38	
39	### Trigger
40	
41	```
42	/resell-au refresh <folder>
43	```
44	
45	If no folder is given, default to `~/Desktop/things-for-sale/`.
46	
47	### Classification rules
48	
49	For each subfolder (skip names starting with `.` or `_`):
50	
51	| Condition | Classification | In table? |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| no `listing.md` | `not-published` | silent skip |
54	| `**Status:** Sold` | `sold` | silent skip |
55	| `**Status:** Published` + `**Date:**` ≥ 7 days old + `**URL:**` present | `refresh-eligible` | yes |
56	| `**Status:** Published` + `**Date:**` < 7 days old | `too-fresh` | yes, action = "too-fresh, skip" |
57	| `**Status:** Published` + no `**URL:**` line | `no-url` | yes, action = "no URL — paste required" |
58	
59	Silent skips are surfaced as a count summary above the candidate table
60	("Silently skipped: N items") so the operator can spot-check that the
61	right things were ignored.
62	
63	### Parser contracts
64	
65	`listing.md`'s canonical format is produced by Folder Mode Phase 4.
66	The Phase R0 classifier uses **strict regex contracts** — anything
67	that does not match is treated as missing rather than guessed at. The
68	worst classification error is a false-positive `refresh-eligible` that
69	deletes a wrong listing, so the parser errs on the side of "skip".
70	
71	| Field | Regex | Source line |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| Status | `^\*\*Status:\*\*\s+(\S+)` | `**Status:** Published` |
74	| Date | `^\*\*Date:\*\*\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` | `**Date:** 2026-05-21` |
75	| URL | `^\*\*URL:\*\*\s+(\S+)` | `**URL:** https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/...` |
76	| Price | `^\*\*Price:\*\*\s+\$(\d+)` | `**Price:** $140 ono` |
77	| Floor | `Floor:\s*\$(\d+)` | `- Target: ~$130 | Floor: $110 | Garage sale: $70` |
78	
79	Date format is **ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` only.** Anything else means the file
80	was hand-edited and is classified as `not-published` (silent skip).
81	
82	### Proposed-price preview
83	
84	For `refresh-eligible` and `no-url` items, R0 previews the proposed
85	new price using the **default rule** — `−10% clamp-to-floor`, rounded
86	with the seller-rounding rules from the Pricing model. Both R0
87	preview and the Phase R2 final price flow through the same calculator
88	at `scripts/refresh_pricing.py` so the operator sees in R0 exactly
89	what gets posted in R2.
90	
91	If `Floor:` is absent from seller notes, the floor falls back to
92	`list_price × 0.85` (matches Pricing model § 5). The clamp still
93	holds.
94	
95	For `too-fresh` rows, the table shows `—` for proposed price and
96	floor — no decision is being made on these items this session.
97	
98	The floor gate (next section) is where the operator confirms or
99	overrides the previewed price before Phase R1 runs.
100	
101	### Session cap (5 per session)
102	
103	If more than 5 items are `refresh-eligible`:
104	* Sort by age (oldest first).
105	* Take the oldest 5 as the queued set.
106	* Show the rest under `deferred to next session` in the table, with
107	  a count summary in the "### Deferred to next session" section.
108	
109	The cap is FB rate-limit hygiene — bursts >5 refreshes/hour are the
110	shadowban signal in reseller-community data. Re-run the skill after
111	≥30 minutes to drain the deferred set.
112	
113	### Floor gate (the operator-confirmation step)
114	
115	After R0 prints the candidate table and the `no-url` paste pass
116	completes, the skill runs the **floor gate** before handing off to
117	Phase R1. The operator can accept all defaults, override per item, or
118	override in bulk.
119	
120	**Per-item overrides** (one line per item, in any order):
121	
122	| Operator input | Meaning |
123	|---|---|
124	| no response, or item not mentioned | accept the previewed `-10% clamp-to-floor` price |
125	| `<item>: same` | keep the current price (no drop) — useful when comps suggest the price is already right |
126	| `<item>: $X` | set the new price to `$X`, **still clamped to the floor** — operator's number overrides the calculator, the floor stays non-negotiable |
127	
128	**Bulk overrides** (apply to every `refresh-eligible` item in the queued
129	set, not the deferred ones):
130	
131	| Operator input | Meaning |
132	|---|---|
133	| `drop everything N%` | apply `−N%` instead of the default `−10%`, then clamp each item to its own floor |
134	| `keep all prices` | equivalent to `drop everything 0%` — recreate every item at its current price |
135	
136	Resolution order when both kinds of input arrive:
137	
138	1. Apply the bulk rate first (sets the new baseline for every item).
139	2. Apply per-item overrides on top (a per-item `$X` wins over the bulk rate; `same` wins over the bulk rate too).
140	3. Clamp every result to its floor as the last step — the floor is the only invariant the operator cannot override.
141	
142	Operationally the calculator is one function call per item via
143	`scripts/refresh_pricing.py`:
144	
145	```python
146	proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.10)   # default
147	proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.15)   # "drop everything 15%"
148	proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.0)    # "same" / "keep all prices"
149	clamp_to_floor(x, floor, current)                # per-item "$X" override
150	```
151	
152	The CLI mirrors the Python API for shell-debug:
153	
154	```bash
155	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_pricing.py --current 40 --floor 35
156	# 35
157	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_pricing.py --current 100 --floor 80 --drop 0.15
158	# 85
159	```
160	
161	After the floor gate resolves, re-print the queued set as a
162	post-gate confirmation table — same columns, but the `Proposed`
163	column reflects the resolved prices and a new `Drop` column shows
164	the realised percentage (so the operator can spot floor-clamp
165	saves: `$40 → $35 (drop 12.5%, floor)`). The operator confirms once,
166	then Phase R1 begins.
167	
168	### Interaction with the live-price override
169	
170	The live-price override runs **before** the floor gate. It updates
171	the "current price" the calculator sees, in-memory only — `listing.md`
172	is never written back. Sequence:
173	
174	1. R0 classifier reads `**Price:**` from each `listing.md`. This is
175	   the *snapshot at publish time*, not always the live FB price.
176	2. Live-price override prompt: operator pastes `<item>: $X` per
177	   item where the live FB price has drifted from the snapshot.
178	3. Floor gate: defaults and overrides are computed against the
179	   live price from step 2, not the snapshot.
180	
181	This ordering matters: an item published at $50, manually dropped
182	to $35 on FB, with floor $30, should refresh at `max(30, round(35 ×
183	0.9)) = max(30, round(31.5)) = $30` — not at `max(30, round(50 ×
184	0.9)) = $45`, which would be a *price increase*, the opposite of
185	what a refresh is for.
186	
187	### `no-url` interaction
188	
189	When an item is classified `no-url`, the skill prompts the user to
190	paste the listing's FB URL during Phase R0. **The paste is in-memory
191	for the current session only — never written back to `listing.md`.**
192	
193	If the user wants the URL persisted, they need to add the `**URL:**`
194	line manually. A missing URL line in the file is the signal that
195	capture failed at publish time (consistent with the Folder Mode
196	Phase 4 Step 6 rule: omit rather than write a placeholder).
197	
198	### Re-running is identical (no side effects)
199	
200	Phase R0 writes nothing. Re-running on the same folder on the same
201	day, with the same listings, produces the same table. This is the
202	hand-test invariant for the slice.
203	
204	## Output: the candidate table
205	
206	```
207	⚠️  Refresh = delete + relist on FB Marketplace.
208	    DELETE LOSES: saves, chat history, view count.
209	    This is the established tactic for resetting the FB algorithm; the loss is the price.
210	
211	Found 10 items: 5 queued, 1 deferred, 1 no-url, 1 too-fresh, 2 silently skipped (sold or no listing.md).
212	
213	## Candidate table
214	
215	| Item | Age | Current | Proposed | Floor | Action |
216	|------|-----|---------|----------|-------|--------|
217	| eligible-60d | 60d | $50 | $45 | $35 | refresh |
218	| eligible-30d | 30d | $100 | $90 | $70 | refresh |
219	| ...
220	| too-fresh-3d | 3d | $40 | — | — | too-fresh, skip |
221	| eligible-8d | 8d | $25 | $22 | $20 | deferred to next session |
222	
223	### Deferred to next session (1 item)
224	Rate-limit hygiene caps refresh at 5 per session.
225	Re-run `/resell-au refresh ...` after ≥30 minutes to drain the queue.
226	```
227	
228	The data-loss warning prints **exactly once per session** — the start
229	of Phase R0, above the table. Each `/resell-au refresh ...` invocation
230	is one session; subsequent invocations re-print it.
231	
232	## Running the classifier
233	
234	The R0 classifier is implemented as a Python script so the parsing is
235	deterministic and regression-testable. Invoke it directly rather than
236	re-implementing the rules inline — the script is the single source of
237	truth for what counts as `refresh-eligible`.
238	
239	```bash
240	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_r0_classify.py <target_folder>
241	```
242	
243	For deterministic fixture testing, set `REFRESH_R0_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`
244	to override the "today" date so age classifications stay stable across
245	runs.
246	
247	## Phase R2 — recreate at new price
248	
249	Phase R2 runs after R1 has confirmed deletion for the current item
250	(`status: deleted` in the run-state JSON, `delete_detection`
251	populated). One item at a time — multi-item batching and resume
252	semantics are documented in § "Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop". The
253	recreate price comes from the R0 floor-gate resolution (default
254	−10% clamp-to-floor, with per-item and bulk overrides) rather than
255	the listing's snapshot.
256	
257	R2 reuses Folder Mode Phase 4 Steps 1–6 verbatim — the recreate
258	form is the same `/marketplace/create/item` flow regardless of
259	whether it's a brand-new listing or a refresh. The only differences
260	are (a) **pre-fill data comes from `listing.md`** rather than from
261	Phase 1 photo-drafted output, and (b) on success, the `listing.md`
262	updater (`scripts/refresh_listing_md_update.py`) runs instead of the
263	Phase 4 writer.
264	
265	### Pre-conditions
266	
267	- Phase R1 ran on this item with terminal state `status: deleted`
268	  and `delete_detection ∈ {redirect, listing_gone_copy, row_missing}`.
269	  R2 must NOT run if deletion was unconfirmed
270	  (`delete_detection: "timeout_manual"`) — duplicate-listing risk is
271	  the whole reason R1 stop-the-lines.
272	- Recreate price (`new_price`) is decided by the R0 floor gate.
273	  `old_price` for the refresh-history bullet is the operator-confirmed
274	  live price (live-price override if provided, else `**Price:**`
275	  snapshot from `listing.md`). When the floor gate resolves to the
276	  same value as the live price (e.g. operator typed `same`, or
277	  `−10%` clamped exactly to floor and floor == current), `old_price`
278	  and `new_price` match and the bullet reads `$X → $X`.
279	
280	### Step R2.1 — pre-fill the form payload from listing.md
281	
282	Parse the item's `listing.md` for the recreate inputs:
283	
284	| Phase 4 field | Source line in listing.md |
285	|---|---|
286	| Title | `**Title:**` in `## Ad copy` |
287	| Price | resolved `new_price` from the R0 floor gate (default `proposed_price(current, floor)`, per-item or bulk override applied) |
288	| Category | `**Category:**` in `## Ad copy` |
289	| Condition | `**Condition:**` in `## Ad copy` |
290	| Description | `**Description:**` body in `## Ad copy` |
291	| Location | `**Location:**` in `## Ad copy` |
292	| Photos | every image file in the item's subfolder, in lexical filename order |
293	
294	Photos are not recorded in `listing.md` — they live on disk in the
295	same subfolder Folder Mode Phase 4 originally uploaded from, so a
296	lexical-order listing of `.jpg` / `.jpeg` / `.png` / `.heic` files
297	gives the same photo set. Cap 10 — same as Phase 4.
298	
299	### Step R2.2 — drive the recreate (Phase 4 Steps 1–6)
300	
301	Run `browser-automation.md` § "The loop (one item, one platform)"
302	Steps 1 through 6 verbatim (including Step 6b). The outcome is one of:
303	
304	- `post_publish_detection: "url_match"` — new listing URL captured
305	  directly from the post-publish redirect.
306	- `post_publish_detection: "iframe_extract"` — the publish landed on the
307	  your-listings page or timed out, and Step 6b recovered the real URL from
308	  the Selling-page ad-preview iframe (verified by exact title match).
309	- `post_publish_detection: "your_listings_redirect"` or
310	  `"timeout_manual"` — Publish click landed, but neither the polling loop
311	  nor the Step 6b iframe recovery captured the URL. Ask the operator to
312	  paste it, same flow as Phase 4 Step 6.
313	
314	If the recreate fails at any step (snapshot mismatch, captcha,
315	publish timeout with no URL pasted by the operator):
316	
317	- **Do NOT touch `listing.md`.** Leaving it alone means the next
318	  run sees this item as `no-url` (since no URL was captured) and the
319	  operator can hand-fix or retry — the multi-item loop's resume
320	  contract picks up from this state.
321	- Update the run-state JSON to `status: deleted` (not `recreated`)
322	  and populate `failure_reason` with a short string. The multi-item
323	  loop then surfaces the item as `action: manual` on the next
324	  `plan` call.
325	
326	### Step R2.3 — update listing.md
327	
328	When a new URL is available (from `url_match`, `iframe_extract`, or
329	operator paste), run the updater:
330	
331	```bash
332	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_listing_md_update.py \
333	    <item_subfolder>/listing.md \
334	    --old-url   "<old URL from run-state>" \
335	    --new-url   "<new URL>" \
336	    --age-days  <age_days from run-state> \
337	    --old-price <old_price from run-state> \
338	    --new-price <new_price from run-state>
339	```
340	
341	`old_price` is the live-confirmed price the listing was running at
342	before the refresh; `new_price` is the floor-gate-resolved price the
343	recreate posted at. They differ when the drop took effect (typical
344	case) and match when the operator chose `same` or the floor clamp
345	caught a drop that would have been smaller than the rounding band.
346	
347	The script (deterministic, byte-identical on Comps):
348	
349	- Replaces `**URL:**` with the new URL (inserts the line after
350	  `**Platform:**` if absent — the `no-url` paste-in-R0 case).
351	- Replaces `**Date:**` with today (`REFRESH_R2_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`
352	  overrides for deterministic tests).
353	- Leaves `**Price:**` byte-identical.
354	- Creates or appends `## Refresh history` between `## Seller notes`
355	  and `## Comps`, adding one bullet:
356	  ```
357	  - YYYY-MM-DD (refresh #N): $X → $Y. Old URL: <old>. New URL: <new>. Age at refresh: Nd.
358	  ```
359	  The refresh number increments from any existing `(refresh #N)`
360	  bullet in the section.
361	- Refuses to write if the `## Comps` block (heading to end-of-file)
362	  is not byte-identical — internal safety guard against the
363	  refresh history insertion accidentally clobbering captured comp
364	  data.
365	
366	Pass `--dry-run` to print to stdout instead of mutating the file
367	(used by the regression tests in `tests/check_refresh_r2.sh`).
368	
369	### Step R2.4 — finalise run-state
370	
371	On successful update:
372	
373	```
374	status: recreated
375	new_url: <captured URL>
376	```
377	
378	`delete_detection` was already populated by R1 and is carried
379	forward unchanged.
380	
381	## Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop
382	
383	After R0 produces the queued set (up to 5 items, oldest-first) and
384	the operator confirms the floor gate, the skill runs R1 then R2 for
385	each queued item in order, with **30–90 s human-cadence delays**
386	between items. The loop is driven off the Refresh Mode run-state
387	JSON file, which is **the single source of truth** for what each
388	item's next action is — both for the in-session loop and for
389	resuming after a crash, `/compact`, or the user killing the session.
390	
391	The orchestration script is `scripts/refresh_runstate.py`. It has
392	three subcommands; the agent's loop is built on `init` (start or
393	resume), `plan` (what's next), `update` (record the result).
394	
395	### Step M0 — init or resume the run-state file
396	
397	After the floor gate, build a queued items array and pass it to
398	`init`. The script's behaviour is the resume contract:
399	
400	```bash
401	# JSON file with one object per queued item — see schema below.
402	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py init <target_folder> \
403	    --queued-json /tmp/queued.json
404	```
405	
406	| Folder state | What init does |
407	|---|---|
408	| No `.resell-au-refresh-*.json` in folder | Create a new file `<folder>/.resell-au-refresh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.json` seeded from `--queued-json`. Print its path. |
409	| Latest file has any item in `pending`, `deleted`, or `failed` | **Resume** — print the existing file's path, ignore `--queued-json`. This is the load-bearing rule for the "kill mid-flight + restart" path. |
410	| Latest file has all items in `recreated` / `skipped` | Treat as new run — create a new file from `--queued-json`. (The drained-queue-then-add-more case.) |
411	| Latest file unreadable (JSON corrupted) | Exit non-zero. Do not silently overwrite — the operator may want to recover it. |
412	
413	**The same run-state file is updated in place across resumes.** A
414	restart never produces a new timestamped file — `init` returns the
415	existing path, the loop continues mutating it.
416	
417	The queued-item JSON shape (the agent assembles this from R0's
418	classified set + the floor-gate-resolved prices, then feeds it to
419	init):
420	
421	```json
422	[
423	  {
424	    "subfolder": "kettlebell",
425	    "title": "12kg Kettlebell — like new",
426	    "old_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/111/",
427	    "old_price": 45,
428	    "new_price": 40,
429	    "floor": 35,
430	    "age_days": 12,
431	    "refresh_count_before": 0
432	  }
433	]
434	```
435	
436	`refresh_count_before` is optional (defaults to 0) and informational
437	only — the listing.md updater derives the canonical refresh number
438	from existing `## Refresh history` bullets in the file, so this
439	field doesn't need to be accurate.
440	
441	### Step M1 — defer-notice before R1 starts
442	
443	Before the first R1 begins, print the defer notice **exactly once**
444	per session, naming the deferred items so the operator knows what
445	will be left over. R0 already shows the deferred set in the
446	candidate table; this is the "confirming what I'm about to do"
447	message at the start of execution:
448	
449	```
450	Processing 5 items this session. Deferred to next session
451	(≥30 min from now): eligible-8d, eligible-9d.
452	Re-run `/resell-au refresh <folder>` after the cooldown to drain them.
453	```
454	
455	If zero items are deferred, skip the message entirely — no value
456	in noise.
457	
458	### Step M2 — loop on `plan` until no `r1`/`r2` actions remain
459	
460	Each iteration calls `plan`, which emits one JSON object per item
461	(newline-delimited) with a `status` and a derived `action`:
462	
463	```bash
464	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py plan <runstate_path>
465	```
466	
467	| `status` in run-state | `action` from plan | Loop branches to |
468	|---|---|---|
469	| `pending` | `r1` | R1 delete loop in `browser-automation.md` → on success, `update --status deleted`; on confirmed deletion failure, `update --status failed` |
470	| `deleted` | `r2` | R2 recreate (§ "Phase R2 — recreate at new price" above) — **do NOT re-run R1**, the old listing is already gone (would 404) |
471	| `recreated` | `done` | Skip — item already finished in this run-state |
472	| `skipped` | `done` | Skip — operator-decided terminal |
473	| `failed` | `manual` | Surface the item + `failure_reason` to the operator; do not auto-retry. Operator can edit the run-state file by hand or re-run R0 once the underlying issue is fixed. |
474	
475	Take the first item whose action is `r1` or `r2`, run that phase,
476	update the run-state, then sleep 30–90 s (random) using
477	`run_in_background: true` on a Bash `sleep` — same pattern as Phase
478	4 Step 7 / R1.8. After the sleep, re-run `plan` and continue.
479	The loop terminates when no items have action `r1` or `r2` left.
480	
481	The per-item delay applies between **items**, not between R1 and R2
482	of the same item — R1 hands directly to R2 once deletion is
483	confirmed, with no inter-phase delay (per the Phase R2 pre-condition
484	that the delete confirmation be recent and unambiguous).
485	
486	### Step M3 — update after each phase
487	
488	After a phase resolves, write the result back:
489	
490	```bash
491	# Successful deletion.
492	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
493	    --item 0 --status deleted --delete-detection redirect
494	
495	# Successful recreate.
496	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
497	    --item 0 --status recreated --new-url "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/"
498	
499	# Confirmed failure (e.g. deletion timeout, operator picked "continue" to skip).
500	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
501	    --item 0 --status failed --failure-reason "delete timeout — operator skipped"
502	```
503	
504	`update` is atomic (temp + rename) so a kill mid-write can't
505	corrupt the file. The corresponding `*_at` field
506	(`pending_at` / `deleted_at` / `recreated_at` / `skipped_at` /
507	`failed_at`) is auto-stamped on every status transition —
508	`pending_at` is stamped by `init` at creation time. The
509	timestamps let the operator verify the 30–90 s inter-item gap
510	from the file alone, no shell history needed.
511	
512	### Resume in practice
513	
514	Headline scenario: kill the run after item 0 is `deleted` but before
515	`recreated`, re-invoke `/resell-au refresh <folder>`. The skill then:
516	
517	1. Calls `init <folder>` (no `--queued-json` needed) — picks up
518	   the existing `.resell-au-refresh-…json`.
519	2. Calls `plan` — item 0 has `action: r2` (resume from recreate;
520	   the old listing is already gone), items 1+ have `action: r1`.
521	3. Runs R2 for item 0 first (no R1 re-run, no 404 risk), then
522	   R1+R2 for the rest, with 30–90 s gaps between items.
523	4. The same run-state file ends up with every item at `recreated`
524	   — **never a new file per resume**.
525	
526	## Refresh Mode run-state file
527	
528	Written to `<target_folder>/.resell-au-refresh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.json`
529	by `scripts/refresh_runstate.py init` at the start of the R1+R2
530	loop. Refresh runs use a separate file from Folder Mode runs because
531	the per-item shape differs (no comp block, no platforms map —
532	refresh is single-platform, single-action).
533	
534	```json
535	{
536	  "run_started": "ISO 8601 timestamp",
537	  "target_folder": "/path/to/folder",
538	  "session_cap": 5,
539	  "items": [
540	    {
541	      "subfolder": "kettlebell",
542	      "title": "12kg Kettlebell — like new",
543	      "old_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/111/",
544	      "old_price": 45,
545	      "new_price": 40,
546	      "floor": 35,
547	      "age_days": 12,
548	      "refresh_count_before": 0,
549	      "status": "pending | deleted | recreated | failed | skipped",
550	      "delete_detection": "redirect | listing_gone_copy | row_missing | timeout_manual | null",
551	      "new_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/ | null",
552	      "failure_reason": "string | null",
553	      "pending_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
554	      "deleted_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
555	      "recreated_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
556	      "skipped_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
557	      "failed_at": "ISO 8601 | null"
558	    }
559	  ]
560	}
561	```
562	
563	Resume semantics:
564	
565	| Terminal state | Meaning |
566	|---|---|
567	| `pending` | Not started — R1 has not yet deleted. Resume from R1. |
568	| `deleted` | R1 succeeded but R2 did not capture a new URL. Resume from R2 — the OLD listing is already gone. Do not re-run R1 (would 404). |
569	| `recreated` | R2 succeeded, `listing.md` updated. Item is done. |
570	| `skipped` | Operator-decided skip (e.g. unrecoverable mismatch). Do not retry. |
571	| `failed` | Phase failed and operator has not yet decided next step. Re-running `init` will resume the file; `plan` surfaces these as `action: manual` so the operator chooses (edit run-state by hand, or fix the underlying issue and re-run). |
572	
573	The `pending_at` / `deleted_at` / `recreated_at` / `skipped_at` /
574	`failed_at` fields are auto-stamped by
575	`scripts/refresh_runstate.py` — `pending_at` at `init` time,
576	the rest on each `update` call. The inter-item-delay
577	verification (each item-to-item gap between 30 and 90 s) works
578	off the file alone — no shell history needed.
579	
580	`session_cap` is written into the run-state at `init` for
581	observability (it tells anyone inspecting the file "this run was
582	capped at 5"). The cap is enforced in two places: upstream in
583	`refresh_r0_classify.py` (trims eligible items to `SESSION_CAP`
584	before writing `--queued-json`), and defensively in
585	`refresh_runstate.py init` (refuses `--queued-json` arrays longer
586	than `SESSION_CAP` with a non-zero exit). The double enforcement
587	guards against an R0 regression silently passing too many items to
588	the loop. `refresh_count_before` is similarly informational; the
589	listing.md updater derives the canonical refresh number from
590	existing `## Refresh history` bullets in the file rather than
591	trusting this field.
592	
593	## Phase R3 — summary output
594	
595	After the multi-item loop drains (every queued item has terminal
596	status `recreated` / `failed` / `skipped`), Phase R3 reads the
597	run-state JSON and prints one summary block to the user. R3 is
598	read-only: no further `listing.md` updates, no browser actions.
599	
600	### Output format
601	
602	```
603	## Refresh summary
604	
605	5 items processed: 4 refreshed, 0 skipped, 1 failed.
606	
607	| Item | Status | Detail |
608	|------|--------|--------|
609	| kettlebell | refreshed | $45 → $40 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/ (was 111) |
610	| ikea-rugs  | refreshed | $40 → $35 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/444/ (was 333) |
611	| violin     | refreshed | $100 → $90 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/666/ (was 555) |
612	| bookshelf  | refreshed | $80 → $72 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/888/ (was 777) |
613	| chair      | failed    | delete timeout — operator skipped |
614	
615	Deferred to next session (2 items, re-run after ≥30 min):
616	- couch (10d)
617	- mirror (8d)
618	```
619	
620	### Per-row composition
621	
622	| Run-state `status` | Row "Status" | Row "Detail" |
623	|---|---|---|
624	| `recreated` | `refreshed` | `$<old_price> → $<new_price> — <new_url> (was <old_id>)` where `<old_id>` is the digits in `old_url` between `/marketplace/item/` and the trailing `/` |
625	| `skipped` | `skipped` | `failure_reason` verbatim (operator-typed at the stop-the-line `continue` prompt) |
626	| `failed` | `failed` | `failure_reason` verbatim |
627	| `pending` / `deleted` | — | should not appear at R3 — loop only exits on terminal states. If present, the loop terminated abnormally; surface a stop-the-line message instead of the summary table |
628	
629	### Deferred section
630	
631	The R0-classified items that were over the 5-per-session cap are not
632	in the run-state JSON (only the queued 5 are). R3 sources them from
633	the R0 classifier output retained in memory for the session. Format
634	is `<subfolder> (<age_days>d)` per line, sorted oldest-first to
635	match R0's queueing order.
636	
637	If zero items were deferred, **omit the entire `Deferred to next
638	session` section** — no value in printing empty noise.
639	
640	### Total processed count
641	
642	Header counts come from the run-state items array — total = items in
643	the run-state (not including R0-deferred items). The sum of
644	refreshed + skipped + failed equals total processed.
645	
646	## Tests and fixtures
647	
648	All scripts ship with deterministic fixtures or unit tests so the
649	contracts above are regression-checked. Run after touching the
650	matching script.
651	
652	| Script | Tests | Invocation | Env override |
653	|---|---|---|---|
654	| `refresh_r0_classify.py` | `tests/fixtures/refresh-r0/` (golden diff covering all 5 buckets + cap deferral) | `bash tests/check_refresh_r0.sh` | `REFRESH_R0_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD` |
655	| `refresh_listing_md_update.py` | `tests/fixtures/refresh-r2/` (3 cases: first-refresh-with-comps, second-refresh, no-url-no-comps) | `bash tests/check_refresh_r2.sh` | `REFRESH_R2_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD` |
656	| `refresh_pricing.py` | `tests/test_refresh_pricing.py` (unittest: acceptance cases, per-item + bulk overrides, rounding bands, absent-floor fallback) | `bash tests/check_refresh_pricing.sh` | — |
657	| `refresh_runstate.py` | `tests/test_refresh_runstate.py` (unittest: status-action mapping, `*_at` auto-stamp, find-latest, filename format, init CLI integration) | `bash tests/check_refresh_runstate.sh` | `REFRESH_RUNSTATE_NOW=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` |
658	
659	The fixtures are parser-correctness only. End-to-end verification —
660	the real eval — is a hand-run against `~/Desktop/things-for-sale/`
661	with the candidate table and summary table sanity-checked against
662	what the operator expects.
663

# Refresh strategy

When the user runs `/resell-au refresh <folder>`, the skill enters
**Refresh Mode** — a third top-level mode alongside Text Mode and
Folder Mode. Refresh Mode delete-and-relists stale FB Marketplace
listings to reset the FB algorithm's "honeymoon" visibility window.

This file is the single home for refresh-only reference detail. Phase
index (all sections live below):

| Phase | What it does | Where to read |
|---|---|---|
| R0 | Discovery & classification (read-only) — candidate table, session cap, floor gate | § "Phase R0 — discovery & classification" |
| R1 | Delete existing listing on FB | `browser-automation.md` § "Refresh Mode — Phase R1 delete loop"; locators in `facebook-marketplace.md` § "Delete listing locators" |
| R2 | Recreate at new price + update `listing.md` | § "Phase R2 — recreate at new price"; scripts: `refresh_listing_md_update.py`, `refresh_pricing.py` |
| Multi-item loop | Session cap, inter-item delays, resume on restart | § "Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop"; script: `refresh_runstate.py` |
| R3 | Summary table | § "Phase R3 — summary output" |

## Why delete-and-relist

FB Marketplace gives every new listing a 24–48 hour "honeymoon" of
aggressive feed visibility. After a few days, visibility drops sharply.
The established reseller tactic — confirmed across 2024–2026
reseller-community research — is to **delete the stale listing and
recreate it with a fresh price.** Empirically this produces a ~30%
message-rate lift vs the native "Renew" button.

Trade-off: deleting loses **saves, chat history, and view count.** The
skill prints a one-line data-loss warning at the top of Phase R0 so
the user is reminded before confirming the candidate table.

## Phase R0 — discovery & classification

Phase R0 is read-only: walk the target folder, parse each subfolder's
`listing.md`, and produce a candidate table. No browser actions in
this phase other than the existing Chrome login check from Folder Mode
Phase 0.

### Trigger

```
/resell-au refresh <folder>
```

If no folder is given, default to `~/Desktop/things-for-sale/`.

### Classification rules

For each subfolder (skip names starting with `.` or `_`):

| Condition | Classification | In table? |
|---|---|---|
| no `listing.md` | `not-published` | silent skip |
| `**Status:** Sold` | `sold` | silent skip |
| `**Status:** Published` + `**Date:**` ≥ 7 days old + `**URL:**` present | `refresh-eligible` | yes |
| `**Status:** Published` + `**Date:**` < 7 days old | `too-fresh` | yes, action = "too-fresh, skip" |
| `**Status:** Published` + no `**URL:**` line | `no-url` | yes, action = "no URL — paste required" |

Silent skips are surfaced as a count summary above the candidate table
("Silently skipped: N items") so the operator can spot-check that the
right things were ignored.

### Parser contracts

`listing.md`'s canonical format is produced by Folder Mode Phase 4.
The Phase R0 classifier uses **strict regex contracts** — anything
that does not match is treated as missing rather than guessed at. The
worst classification error is a false-positive `refresh-eligible` that
deletes a wrong listing, so the parser errs on the side of "skip".

| Field | Regex | Source line |
|---|---|---|
| Status | `^\*\*Status:\*\*\s+(\S+)` | `**Status:** Published` |
| Date | `^\*\*Date:\*\*\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` | `**Date:** 2026-05-21` |
| URL | `^\*\*URL:\*\*\s+(\S+)` | `**URL:** https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/...` |
| Price | `^\*\*Price:\*\*\s+\$(\d+)` | `**Price:** $140 ono` |
| Floor | `Floor:\s*\$(\d+)` | `- Target: ~$130 | Floor: $110 | Garage sale: $70` |

Date format is **ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` only.** Anything else means the file
was hand-edited and is classified as `not-published` (silent skip).

### Proposed-price preview

For `refresh-eligible` and `no-url` items, R0 previews the proposed
new price using the **default rule** — `−10% clamp-to-floor`, rounded
with the seller-rounding rules from the Pricing model. Both R0
preview and the Phase R2 final price flow through the same calculator
at `scripts/refresh_pricing.py` so the operator sees in R0 exactly
what gets posted in R2.

If `Floor:` is absent from seller notes, the floor falls back to
`list_price × 0.85` (matches Pricing model § 5). The clamp still
holds.

For `too-fresh` rows, the table shows `—` for proposed price and
floor — no decision is being made on these items this session.

The floor gate (next section) is where the operator confirms or
overrides the previewed price before Phase R1 runs.

### Session cap (5 per session)

If more than 5 items are `refresh-eligible`:
* Sort by age (oldest first).
* Take the oldest 5 as the queued set.
* Show the rest under `deferred to next session` in the table, with
  a count summary in the "### Deferred to next session" section.

The cap is FB rate-limit hygiene — bursts >5 refreshes/hour are the
shadowban signal in reseller-community data. Re-run the skill after
≥30 minutes to drain the deferred set.

### Floor gate (the operator-confirmation step)

After R0 prints the candidate table and the `no-url` paste pass
completes, the skill runs the **floor gate** before handing off to
Phase R1. The operator can accept all defaults, override per item, or
override in bulk.

**Per-item overrides** (one line per item, in any order):

| Operator input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| no response, or item not mentioned | accept the previewed `-10% clamp-to-floor` price |
| `<item>: same` | keep the current price (no drop) — useful when comps suggest the price is already right |
| `<item>: $X` | set the new price to `$X`, **still clamped to the floor** — operator's number overrides the calculator, the floor stays non-negotiable |

**Bulk overrides** (apply to every `refresh-eligible` item in the queued
set, not the deferred ones):

| Operator input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `drop everything N%` | apply `−N%` instead of the default `−10%`, then clamp each item to its own floor |
| `keep all prices` | equivalent to `drop everything 0%` — recreate every item at its current price |

Resolution order when both kinds of input arrive:

1. Apply the bulk rate first (sets the new baseline for every item).
2. Apply per-item overrides on top (a per-item `$X` wins over the bulk rate; `same` wins over the bulk rate too).
3. Clamp every result to its floor as the last step — the floor is the only invariant the operator cannot override.

Operationally the calculator is one function call per item via
`scripts/refresh_pricing.py`:

```python
proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.10)   # default
proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.15)   # "drop everything 15%"
proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.0)    # "same" / "keep all prices"
clamp_to_floor(x, floor, current)                # per-item "$X" override
```

The CLI mirrors the Python API for shell-debug:

```bash
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_pricing.py --current 40 --floor 35
# 35
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_pricing.py --current 100 --floor 80 --drop 0.15
# 85
```

After the floor gate resolves, re-print the queued set as a
post-gate confirmation table — same columns, but the `Proposed`
column reflects the resolved prices and a new `Drop` column shows
the realised percentage (so the operator can spot floor-clamp
saves: `$40 → $35 (drop 12.5%, floor)`). The operator confirms once,
then Phase R1 begins.

### Interaction with the live-price override

The live-price override runs **before** the floor gate. It updates
the "current price" the calculator sees, in-memory only — `listing.md`
is never written back. Sequence:

1. R0 classifier reads `**Price:**` from each `listing.md`. This is
   the *snapshot at publish time*, not always the live FB price.
2. Live-price override prompt: operator pastes `<item>: $X` per
   item where the live FB price has drifted from the snapshot.
3. Floor gate: defaults and overrides are computed against the
   live price from step 2, not the snapshot.

This ordering matters: an item published at $50, manually dropped
to $35 on FB, with floor $30, should refresh at `max(30, round(35 ×
0.9)) = max(30, round(31.5)) = $30` — not at `max(30, round(50 ×
0.9)) = $45`, which would be a *price increase*, the opposite of
what a refresh is for.

### `no-url` interaction

When an item is classified `no-url`, the skill prompts the user to
paste the listing's FB URL during Phase R0. **The paste is in-memory
for the current session only — never written back to `listing.md`.**

If the user wants the URL persisted, they need to add the `**URL:**`
line manually. A missing URL line in the file is the signal that
capture failed at publish time (consistent with the Folder Mode
Phase 4 Step 6 rule: omit rather than write a placeholder).

### Re-running is identical (no side effects)

Phase R0 writes nothing. Re-running on the same folder on the same
day, with the same listings, produces the same table. This is the
hand-test invariant for the slice.

## Output: the candidate table

```
⚠️  Refresh = delete + relist on FB Marketplace.
    DELETE LOSES: saves, chat history, view count.
    This is the established tactic for resetting the FB algorithm; the loss is the price.

Found 10 items: 5 queued, 1 deferred, 1 no-url, 1 too-fresh, 2 silently skipped (sold or no listing.md).

## Candidate table

| Item | Age | Current | Proposed | Floor | Action |
|------|-----|---------|----------|-------|--------|
| eligible-60d | 60d | $50 | $45 | $35 | refresh |
| eligible-30d | 30d | $100 | $90 | $70 | refresh |
| ...
| too-fresh-3d | 3d | $40 | — | — | too-fresh, skip |
| eligible-8d | 8d | $25 | $22 | $20 | deferred to next session |

### Deferred to next session (1 item)
Rate-limit hygiene caps refresh at 5 per session.
Re-run `/resell-au refresh ...` after ≥30 minutes to drain the queue.
```

The data-loss warning prints **exactly once per session** — the start
of Phase R0, above the table. Each `/resell-au refresh ...` invocation
is one session; subsequent invocations re-print it.

## Running the classifier

The R0 classifier is implemented as a Python script so the parsing is
deterministic and regression-testable. Invoke it directly rather than
re-implementing the rules inline — the script is the single source of
truth for what counts as `refresh-eligible`.

```bash
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_r0_classify.py <target_folder>
```

For deterministic fixture testing, set `REFRESH_R0_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`
to override the "today" date so age classifications stay stable across
runs.

## Phase R2 — recreate at new price

Phase R2 runs after R1 has confirmed deletion for the current item
(`status: deleted` in the run-state JSON, `delete_detection`
populated). One item at a time — multi-item batching and resume
semantics are documented in § "Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop". The
recreate price comes from the R0 floor-gate resolution (default
−10% clamp-to-floor, with per-item and bulk overrides) rather than
the listing's snapshot.

R2 reuses Folder Mode Phase 4 Steps 1–6 verbatim — the recreate
form is the same `/marketplace/create/item` flow regardless of
whether it's a brand-new listing or a refresh. The only differences
are (a) **pre-fill data comes from `listing.md`** rather than from
Phase 1 photo-drafted output, and (b) on success, the `listing.md`
updater (`scripts/refresh_listing_md_update.py`) runs instead of the
Phase 4 writer.

### Pre-conditions

- Phase R1 ran on this item with terminal state `status: deleted`
  and `delete_detection ∈ {redirect, listing_gone_copy, row_missing}`.
  R2 must NOT run if deletion was unconfirmed
  (`delete_detection: "timeout_manual"`) — duplicate-listing risk is
  the whole reason R1 stop-the-lines.
- Recreate price (`new_price`) is decided by the R0 floor gate.
  `old_price` for the refresh-history bullet is the operator-confirmed
  live price (live-price override if provided, else `**Price:**`
  snapshot from `listing.md`). When the floor gate resolves to the
  same value as the live price (e.g. operator typed `same`, or
  `−10%` clamped exactly to floor and floor == current), `old_price`
  and `new_price` match and the bullet reads `$X → $X`.

### Step R2.1 — pre-fill the form payload from listing.md

Parse the item's `listing.md` for the recreate inputs:

| Phase 4 field | Source line in listing.md |
|---|---|
| Title | `**Title:**` in `## Ad copy` |
| Price | resolved `new_price` from the R0 floor gate (default `proposed_price(current, floor)`, per-item or bulk override applied) |
| Category | `**Category:**` in `## Ad copy` |
| Condition | `**Condition:**` in `## Ad copy` |
| Description | `**Description:**` body in `## Ad copy` |
| Location | `**Location:**` in `## Ad copy` |
| Photos | every image file in the item's subfolder, in lexical filename order |

Photos are not recorded in `listing.md` — they live on disk in the
same subfolder Folder Mode Phase 4 originally uploaded from, so a
lexical-order listing of `.jpg` / `.jpeg` / `.png` / `.heic` files
gives the same photo set. Cap 10 — same as Phase 4.

### Step R2.2 — drive the recreate (Phase 4 Steps 1–6)

Run `browser-automation.md` § "The loop (one item, one platform)"
Steps 1 through 6 verbatim (including Step 6b). The outcome is one of:

- `post_publish_detection: "url_match"` — new listing URL captured
  directly from the post-publish redirect.
- `post_publish_detection: "iframe_extract"` — the publish landed on the
  your-listings page or timed out, and Step 6b recovered the real URL from
  the Selling-page ad-preview iframe (verified by exact title match).
- `post_publish_detection: "your_listings_redirect"` or
  `"timeout_manual"` — Publish click landed, but neither the polling loop
  nor the Step 6b iframe recovery captured the URL. Ask the operator to
  paste it, same flow as Phase 4 Step 6.

If the recreate fails at any step (snapshot mismatch, captcha,
publish timeout with no URL pasted by the operator):

- **Do NOT touch `listing.md`.** Leaving it alone means the next
  run sees this item as `no-url` (since no URL was captured) and the
  operator can hand-fix or retry — the multi-item loop's resume
  contract picks up from this state.
- Update the run-state JSON to `status: deleted` (not `recreated`)
  and populate `failure_reason` with a short string. The multi-item
  loop then surfaces the item as `action: manual` on the next
  `plan` call.

### Step R2.3 — update listing.md

When a new URL is available (from `url_match`, `iframe_extract`, or
operator paste), run the updater:

```bash
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_listing_md_update.py \
    <item_subfolder>/listing.md \
    --old-url   "<old URL from run-state>" \
    --new-url   "<new URL>" \
    --age-days  <age_days from run-state> \
    --old-price <old_price from run-state> \
    --new-price <new_price from run-state>
```

`old_price` is the live-confirmed price the listing was running at
before the refresh; `new_price` is the floor-gate-resolved price the
recreate posted at. They differ when the drop took effect (typical
case) and match when the operator chose `same` or the floor clamp
caught a drop that would have been smaller than the rounding band.

The script (deterministic, byte-identical on Comps):

- Replaces `**URL:**` with the new URL (inserts the line after
  `**Platform:**` if absent — the `no-url` paste-in-R0 case).
- Replaces `**Date:**` with today (`REFRESH_R2_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`
  overrides for deterministic tests).
- Leaves `**Price:**` byte-identical.
- Creates or appends `## Refresh history` between `## Seller notes`
  and `## Comps`, adding one bullet:
  ```
  - YYYY-MM-DD (refresh #N): $X → $Y. Old URL: <old>. New URL: <new>. Age at refresh: Nd.
  ```
  The refresh number increments from any existing `(refresh #N)`
  bullet in the section.
- Refuses to write if the `## Comps` block (heading to end-of-file)
  is not byte-identical — internal safety guard against the
  refresh history insertion accidentally clobbering captured comp
  data.

Pass `--dry-run` to print to stdout instead of mutating the file
(used by the regression tests in `tests/check_refresh_r2.sh`).

### Step R2.4 — finalise run-state

On successful update:

```
status: recreated
new_url: <captured URL>
```

`delete_detection` was already populated by R1 and is carried
forward unchanged.

## Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop

After R0 produces the queued set (up to 5 items, oldest-first) and
the operator confirms the floor gate, the skill runs R1 then R2 for
each queued item in order, with **30–90 s human-cadence delays**
between items. The loop is driven off the Refresh Mode run-state
JSON file, which is **the single source of truth** for what each
item's next action is — both for the in-session loop and for
resuming after a crash, `/compact`, or the user killing the session.

The orchestration script is `scripts/refresh_runstate.py`. It has
three subcommands; the agent's loop is built on `init` (start or
resume), `plan` (what's next), `update` (record the result).

### Step M0 — init or resume the run-state file

After the floor gate, build a queued items array and pass it to
`init`. The script's behaviour is the resume contract:

```bash
# JSON file with one object per queued item — see schema below.
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py init <target_folder> \
    --queued-json /tmp/queued.json
```

| Folder state | What init does |
|---|---|
| No `.resell-au-refresh-*.json` in folder | Create a new file `<folder>/.resell-au-refresh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.json` seeded from `--queued-json`. Print its path. |
| Latest file has any item in `pending`, `deleted`, or `failed` | **Resume** — print the existing file's path, ignore `--queued-json`. This is the load-bearing rule for the "kill mid-flight + restart" path. |
| Latest file has all items in `recreated` / `skipped` | Treat as new run — create a new file from `--queued-json`. (The drained-queue-then-add-more case.) |
| Latest file unreadable (JSON corrupted) | Exit non-zero. Do not silently overwrite — the operator may want to recover it. |

**The same run-state file is updated in place across resumes.** A
restart never produces a new timestamped file — `init` returns the
existing path, the loop continues mutating it.

The queued-item JSON shape (the agent assembles this from R0's
classified set + the floor-gate-resolved prices, then feeds it to
init):

```json
[
  {
    "subfolder": "kettlebell",
    "title": "12kg Kettlebell — like new",
    "old_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/111/",
    "old_price": 45,
    "new_price": 40,
    "floor": 35,
    "age_days": 12,
    "refresh_count_before": 0
  }
]
```

`refresh_count_before` is optional (defaults to 0) and informational
only — the listing.md updater derives the canonical refresh number
from existing `## Refresh history` bullets in the file, so this
field doesn't need to be accurate.

### Step M1 — defer-notice before R1 starts

Before the first R1 begins, print the defer notice **exactly once**
per session, naming the deferred items so the operator knows what
will be left over. R0 already shows the deferred set in the
candidate table; this is the "confirming what I'm about to do"
message at the start of execution:

```
Processing 5 items this session. Deferred to next session
(≥30 min from now): eligible-8d, eligible-9d.
Re-run `/resell-au refresh <folder>` after the cooldown to drain them.
```

If zero items are deferred, skip the message entirely — no value
in noise.

### Step M2 — loop on `plan` until no `r1`/`r2` actions remain

Each iteration calls `plan`, which emits one JSON object per item
(newline-delimited) with a `status` and a derived `action`:

```bash
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py plan <runstate_path>
```

| `status` in run-state | `action` from plan | Loop branches to |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | `r1` | R1 delete loop in `browser-automation.md` → on success, `update --status deleted`; on confirmed deletion failure, `update --status failed` |
| `deleted` | `r2` | R2 recreate (§ "Phase R2 — recreate at new price" above) — **do NOT re-run R1**, the old listing is already gone (would 404) |
| `recreated` | `done` | Skip — item already finished in this run-state |
| `skipped` | `done` | Skip — operator-decided terminal |
| `failed` | `manual` | Surface the item + `failure_reason` to the operator; do not auto-retry. Operator can edit the run-state file by hand or re-run R0 once the underlying issue is fixed. |

Take the first item whose action is `r1` or `r2`, run that phase,
update the run-state, then sleep 30–90 s (random) using
`run_in_background: true` on a Bash `sleep` — same pattern as Phase
4 Step 7 / R1.8. After the sleep, re-run `plan` and continue.
The loop terminates when no items have action `r1` or `r2` left.

The per-item delay applies between **items**, not between R1 and R2
of the same item — R1 hands directly to R2 once deletion is
confirmed, with no inter-phase delay (per the Phase R2 pre-condition
that the delete confirmation be recent and unambiguous).

### Step M3 — update after each phase

After a phase resolves, write the result back:

```bash
# Successful deletion.
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
    --item 0 --status deleted --delete-detection redirect

# Successful recreate.
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
    --item 0 --status recreated --new-url "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/"

# Confirmed failure (e.g. deletion timeout, operator picked "continue" to skip).
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
    --item 0 --status failed --failure-reason "delete timeout — operator skipped"
```

`update` is atomic (temp + rename) so a kill mid-write can't
corrupt the file. The corresponding `*_at` field
(`pending_at` / `deleted_at` / `recreated_at` / `skipped_at` /
`failed_at`) is auto-stamped on every status transition —
`pending_at` is stamped by `init` at creation time. The
timestamps let the operator verify the 30–90 s inter-item gap
from the file alone, no shell history needed.

### Resume in practice

Headline scenario: kill the run after item 0 is `deleted` but before
`recreated`, re-invoke `/resell-au refresh <folder>`. The skill then:

1. Calls `init <folder>` (no `--queued-json` needed) — picks up
   the existing `.resell-au-refresh-…json`.
2. Calls `plan` — item 0 has `action: r2` (resume from recreate;
   the old listing is already gone), items 1+ have `action: r1`.
3. Runs R2 for item 0 first (no R1 re-run, no 404 risk), then
   R1+R2 for the rest, with 30–90 s gaps between items.
4. The same run-state file ends up with every item at `recreated`
   — **never a new file per resume**.

## Refresh Mode run-state file

Written to `<target_folder>/.resell-au-refresh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.json`
by `scripts/refresh_runstate.py init` at the start of the R1+R2
loop. Refresh runs use a separate file from Folder Mode runs because
the per-item shape differs (no comp block, no platforms map —
refresh is single-platform, single-action).

```json
{
  "run_started": "ISO 8601 timestamp",
  "target_folder": "/path/to/folder",
  "session_cap": 5,
  "items": [
    {
      "subfolder": "kettlebell",
      "title": "12kg Kettlebell — like new",
      "old_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/111/",
      "old_price": 45,
      "new_price": 40,
      "floor": 35,
      "age_days": 12,
      "refresh_count_before": 0,
      "status": "pending | deleted | recreated | failed | skipped",
      "delete_detection": "redirect | listing_gone_copy | row_missing | timeout_manual | null",
      "new_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/ | null",
      "failure_reason": "string | null",
      "pending_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
      "deleted_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
      "recreated_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
      "skipped_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
      "failed_at": "ISO 8601 | null"
    }
  ]
}
```

Resume semantics:

| Terminal state | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Not started — R1 has not yet deleted. Resume from R1. |
| `deleted` | R1 succeeded but R2 did not capture a new URL. Resume from R2 — the OLD listing is already gone. Do not re-run R1 (would 404). |
| `recreated` | R2 succeeded, `listing.md` updated. Item is done. |
| `skipped` | Operator-decided skip (e.g. unrecoverable mismatch). Do not retry. |
| `failed` | Phase failed and operator has not yet decided next step. Re-running `init` will resume the file; `plan` surfaces these as `action: manual` so the operator chooses (edit run-state by hand, or fix the underlying issue and re-run). |

The `pending_at` / `deleted_at` / `recreated_at` / `skipped_at` /
`failed_at` fields are auto-stamped by
`scripts/refresh_runstate.py` — `pending_at` at `init` time,
the rest on each `update` call. The inter-item-delay
verification (each item-to-item gap between 30 and 90 s) works
off the file alone — no shell history needed.

`session_cap` is written into the run-state at `init` for
observability (it tells anyone inspecting the file "this run was
capped at 5"). The cap is enforced in two places: upstream in
`refresh_r0_classify.py` (trims eligible items to `SESSION_CAP`
before writing `--queued-json`), and defensively in
`refresh_runstate.py init` (refuses `--queued-json` arrays longer
than `SESSION_CAP` with a non-zero exit). The double enforcement
guards against an R0 regression silently passing too many items to
the loop. `refresh_count_before` is similarly informational; the
listing.md updater derives the canonical refresh number from
existing `## Refresh history` bullets in the file rather than
trusting this field.

## Phase R3 — summary output

After the multi-item loop drains (every queued item has terminal
status `recreated` / `failed` / `skipped`), Phase R3 reads the
run-state JSON and prints one summary block to the user. R3 is
read-only: no further `listing.md` updates, no browser actions.

### Output format

```
## Refresh summary

5 items processed: 4 refreshed, 0 skipped, 1 failed.

| Item | Status | Detail |
|------|--------|--------|
| kettlebell | refreshed | $45 → $40 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/ (was 111) |
| ikea-rugs  | refreshed | $40 → $35 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/444/ (was 333) |
| violin     | refreshed | $100 → $90 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/666/ (was 555) |
| bookshelf  | refreshed | $80 → $72 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/888/ (was 777) |
| chair      | failed    | delete timeout — operator skipped |

Deferred to next session (2 items, re-run after ≥30 min):
- couch (10d)
- mirror (8d)
```

### Per-row composition

| Run-state `status` | Row "Status" | Row "Detail" |
|---|---|---|
| `recreated` | `refreshed` | `$<old_price> → $<new_price> — <new_url> (was <old_id>)` where `<old_id>` is the digits in `old_url` between `/marketplace/item/` and the trailing `/` |
| `skipped` | `skipped` | `failure_reason` verbatim (operator-typed at the stop-the-line `continue` prompt) |
| `failed` | `failed` | `failure_reason` verbatim |
| `pending` / `deleted` | — | should not appear at R3 — loop only exits on terminal states. If present, the loop terminated abnormally; surface a stop-the-line message instead of the summary table |

### Deferred section

The R0-classified items that were over the 5-per-session cap are not
in the run-state JSON (only the queued 5 are). R3 sources them from
the R0 classifier output retained in memory for the session. Format
is `<subfolder> (<age_days>d)` per line, sorted oldest-first to
match R0's queueing order.

If zero items were deferred, **omit the entire `Deferred to next
session` section** — no value in printing empty noise.

### Total processed count

Header counts come from the run-state items array — total = items in
the run-state (not including R0-deferred items). The sum of
refreshed + skipped + failed equals total processed.

## Tests and fixtures

All scripts ship with deterministic fixtures or unit tests so the
contracts above are regression-checked. Run after touching the
matching script.

| Script | Tests | Invocation | Env override |
|---|---|---|---|
| `refresh_r0_classify.py` | `tests/fixtures/refresh-r0/` (golden diff covering all 5 buckets + cap deferral) | `bash tests/check_refresh_r0.sh` | `REFRESH_R0_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `refresh_listing_md_update.py` | `tests/fixtures/refresh-r2/` (3 cases: first-refresh-with-comps, second-refresh, no-url-no-comps) | `bash tests/check_refresh_r2.sh` | `REFRESH_R2_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `refresh_pricing.py` | `tests/test_refresh_pricing.py` (unittest: acceptance cases, per-item + bulk overrides, rounding bands, absent-floor fallback) | `bash tests/check_refresh_pricing.sh` | — |
| `refresh_runstate.py` | `tests/test_refresh_runstate.py` (unittest: status-action mapping, `*_at` auto-stamp, find-latest, filename format, init CLI integration) | `bash tests/check_refresh_runstate.sh` | `REFRESH_RUNSTATE_NOW=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` |

The fixtures are parser-correctness only. End-to-end verification —
the real eval — is a hand-run against `~/Desktop/things-for-sale/`
with the candidate table and summary table sanity-checked against
what the operator expects.

import os, re, json
